input.rationale: Recorded one more sourced relationship from the same feature's plumbing, without claiming a consensus defect or spending an execution: the package's own LogCache wrapper forwards the optional MonotonicLogStore interface but implements no StageCommitIndex or GetCommitIndex, so it does not satisfy CommitTrackingLogStore; because restoreFromCommittedLogs asserts that interface and returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore, enabling RestoreCommittedLogs over a cache-wrapped commit-tracking store makes NewRaft fail with an error that names the cache rather than the underlying store.

knowledge.statement: LogCache wraps a LogStore and forwards five required methods plus a MonotonicLogStore shim (IsMonotonic delegating to the underlying store), but it defines no StageCommitIndex and no GetCommitIndex, so a LogCache value never satisfies CommitTrackingLogStore even when the store it wraps does.
knowledge.conditions: The wrapped store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the wrapper is constructed with NewLogCache and used as the log store of a Raft instance; the interface set of LogCache is fixed at compile time and does not depend on the wrapped value.

knowledge.statement: With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs type-asserts the log store to CommitTrackingLogStore and returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore when the assertion fails, logging "restore committed logs enabled but log store does not support it" with the store's Go type; NewRaft returns that error, so a node whose log store is a LogCache over a commit-tracking store cannot start at all, and the message points at the cache type rather than the capable store underneath. Wrapping is not required for the flag to work: the same underlying store used directly passes the assertion, as the package's own test with InmemCommitTrackingStore shows.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and Config's log store is a LogCache wrapping a store that does implement CommitTrackingLogStore; the failure is a startup error returned by NewRaft, not a runtime behaviour. The package documents that the flag requires a CommitTrackingLogStore and that Raft fails to start otherwise, so this is a fidelity gap between the provided wrapper and the provided optional interface rather than an undocumented consensus path.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration from configuration-carrying log entries only for indices above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); the other writers of r.configurations are snapshot restore, snapshot install and the leader's own appendConfigurationEntry path, and nothing else repairs it.
knowledge.conditions: Startup reconstruction in NewRaft over a log store; lastApplied may already be advanced by restoreFromCommittedLogs or by a restored snapshot; configuration entries are identified by LogConfiguration or the deprecated peer entry types.

knowledge.statement: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the commit index from a CommitTrackingLogStore, clamps it to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs, which applies the committed prefix to the FSM and sets lastApplied to that commit index; this happens after snapshot restore and before NewRaft's configuration scan.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the tracked commit index is at least the index of a configuration entry stored in the log.

knowledge.statement: The configuration a node holds decides its own participation and support arithmetic: runFollower declines to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote in the latest configuration, a candidate needs quorumSize() votes of the latest configuration, and the leader's commitment is constructed from the latest configuration, so a stale or empty reconstruction directly changes which support is required and counted.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is the one reconstructed at startup or later written by a snapshot install or a configuration change; quorumSize and the commitment are computed from configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: appendEntries processes configuration entries only for the entries it newly appends; entries already present at the same index and term are skipped, so ordinary replication from a healthy leader does not re-derive the configuration of a follower whose log already matches.
knowledge.conditions: Follower handling a normal AppendEntries whose entries are duplicates of its own log; entries that are in the leader's compacted prefix instead arrive as an InstallSnapshot, which rewrites both configurations from the snapshot metadata.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across five exercised shapes: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still carried as a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; the demote/promote ladder reported one voter against committed entries of three voters and of five voters; and a peer that had snapshotted itself while still a voter reported three voters after its vote had been removed in the committed configuration, where it holds none. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); the snapshot that supplies the wrong configuration may have been taken by the leader or by the restarting peer itself; no membership change is issued after the restart.

history.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a commit-tracking log store; no other instance left running and no later membership change. knowledge.statement: In the retained live-cluster execution a restarted follower no longer held any configuration and ordinary replication did not repair it: after 400 ms of a leader that stayed in Leader state, the follower's reconstructed configuration was empty (latest_config_index 0, no servers) while its own log's configuration entry at index 103 has two voters and its log already matched the leader's (last log index 113, last applied 110, snapshot_count 0). When that leader afterwards appended a new configuration entry at index 114, the follower's configuration became that entry (latest_config_index 114, three voters), so the repair came from the later configuration change rather than from replication; the flag-disabled control over the same shape held latest_config_index 103 with two voters at observation time and was repaired by the same entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-member cluster whose leader committed a RemoveServer before the restart and kept leading; only the remaining follower was restarted, over its own stores and with no snapshot of its own, reconnected to the live leader in both directions; the observation and repair windows are 400 ms each.

A later receipt produced the same grant without any synthesis, from a peer that campaigned on its own because its reconstruction still granted it a vote, so the caveat now bounds only this earlier execution rather than the finding.

knowledge.statement: In the retained five-voter execution an acknowledged commit was discarded from every store: the restarted holder acknowledged one payload on a single copy of the committed configuration (acknowledged true, reconstructed_config_voters 1 against the five voters recorded at log index 110, holder term 3), the four returning voters elected leadership at term 3 without it, that leader was stopped so the remaining three elected again at term 4, and once the holder was rebuilt the payload was absent from all five stores (copies_after_rejoin 0, payload_on_holder_after false, discarded true, durable_on_majority false); the flag-disabled control could not acknowledge anything at all.
knowledge.conditions: Five-voter cluster whose committed configuration entry sits at log index 110 while the restarted holder's snapshot metadata carries the demoted single-voter configuration (snapshot_config_voters 1); the four returning voters are rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so their configuration comes from their logs; one extra legal election (the first returning leader stopped, the remaining three of five still a quorum) puts the successor leadership in a strictly higher term before the holder rejoins; the payload is searched for in every store across its first-to-last index.

knowledge.statement: In the retained campaign execution a peer that holds no vote in the configuration recorded in its own log acquired leadership on its own initiative: it had snapshotted itself while still a voter (snapshot_config_voters 3), its vote was then removed in the committed configuration (log_config_voters 2, stale_has_vote false), and after both it and the other instance were restarted with the former leader down it reconstructed three voters, campaigned without any external request, and became Leader (campaign_result at parsed index 40: stale_config_voters 3, stale_became_leader true, state Leader) with the other instance — whose own reconstruction held no configuration at all (responder_config_voters 0) — answering one pre-vote and one real vote request from it. The flag-disabled control reconstructed the committed two-voter configuration, held no vote there, sent no request at all and stayed Follower.
knowledge.conditions: Three-member cluster where the campaigning peer took its own snapshot through the public API while still a voter, its vote was then removed by a committed configuration entry, all instances were stopped, and only that peer and one other were restarted with the flag set per case; the former leader stayed down so no known leader could reject the campaign; the restarted peers were reconnected to each other in both directions and the incoming requests were counted by an observer on the answering peer.

func (r *Raft) setupLeaderState() {
	r.leaderState.commitCh = make(chan struct{}, 1)
	r.leaderState.commitment = newCommitment(r.leaderState.commitCh,
		r.configurations.latest,
		r.getLastIndex()+1 /* first index that may be committed in this term */)
	r.leaderState.inflight = list.New()
	r.leaderState.replState = make(map[ServerID]*followerReplication)
	r.leaderState.notify = make(map[*verifyFuture]struct{})
	r.leaderState.stepDown = make(chan struct{}, 1)
}

	PropagateError     bool // If true, return errors instead of calling t.Fatal
}

knowledge.statement: LogCache wraps a LogStore and forwards five required methods plus a MonotonicLogStore shim (IsMonotonic delegating to the underlying store), but it defines no StageCommitIndex and no GetCommitIndex, so a LogCache value never satisfies CommitTrackingLogStore even when the store it wraps does.
knowledge.conditions: The wrapped store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the wrapper is constructed with NewLogCache and used as the log store of a Raft instance; the interface set of LogCache is fixed at compile time and does not depend on the wrapped value.

knowledge.statement: With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs type-asserts the log store to CommitTrackingLogStore and returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore when the assertion fails, logging "restore committed logs enabled but log store does not support it" with the store's Go type; NewRaft returns that error, so a node whose log store is a LogCache over a commit-tracking store cannot start at all, and the message points at the cache type rather than the capable store underneath. Wrapping is not required for the flag to work: the same underlying store used directly passes the assertion, as the package's own test with InmemCommitTrackingStore shows.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and Config's log store is a LogCache wrapping a store that does implement CommitTrackingLogStore; the failure is a startup error returned by NewRaft, not a runtime behaviour. The package documents that the flag requires a CommitTrackingLogStore and that Raft fails to start otherwise, so this is a fidelity gap between the provided wrapper and the provided optional interface rather than an undocumented consensus path.
